Loss of shivering around 30–32 °C is the clinical marker that the body has given up its main heat-producing mechanism, which is why the course flags it as the sign that a patient has slipped from mild into a more dangerous stage. For mild and moderate hypothermia the guideline directs active rewarming: remove wet and cold clothing, cover with dry blankets, use hot packs wrapped in towels, preheat the ambulance interior to 30 °C, and allow mild activity only if appropriate — not a drowsy, slurring patient. Below 28 °C the guideline says not to actively rewarm in the field; insulate, heat the ambulance, and avoid rough handling because the cold myocardium is prone to ventricular fibrillation. Warm-water immersion is not a prehospital intervention at any stage.
questions.explanationZh: BC 考纲把低体温分为轻度（32 °C 以上到 35 °C 以下）、中度（28 °C 以上到 32 °C 以下）、重度（低于 28 °C）。30 °C 属于中度。30–32 °C 左右寒战消失，是身体放弃主要产热机制的临床标志，所以课上把它作为患者从轻度滑入更危险阶段的信号。对轻度和中度低体温，考纲要求主动复温：脱掉湿冷衣物、盖干毯子、用毛巾包裹的热敷袋、救护车车厢预热到 30 °C，只有在合适时才允许轻度活动——嗜睡、言语含糊的患者不合适。低于 28 °C，考纲要求院前不主动复温：保温隔热、车厢加热、避免粗暴搬动，因为冰冷的心肌极易发生室颤。温水浸泡在任何阶段都不是院前措施。

questions.questionEn: A snowmobiler is dug out of an avalanche after 40 minutes. He is unresponsive, rigid and ice-cold, with no obvious breathing. After a 10-second carotid check you feel nothing. What does the BC guideline direct?
questions.questionZh: 一名雪地摩托车手在雪崩 40 分钟后被挖出。他无反应、僵硬、冰冷，看不到明显呼吸。你摸了 10 秒颈动脉，什么也没摸到。BC 考纲要求你怎么做？

options.en: Declare him deceased; 40 minutes of burial is not survivable
options.zh: 宣布死亡；掩埋 40 分钟不可能存活

options.en: Start CPR and shock every time the AED advises, as for any arrest
options.zh: 开始 CPR，AED 每次建议都电击，和普通骤停一样

options.en: Rewarm him actively with hot packs before attempting resuscitation
options.zh: 先用热敷袋主动复温，再尝试复苏

options.en: Pulse check up to 30–45 s, then CPR with up to three shocks
options.zh: 摸脉搏最长 30–45 秒，然后 CPR，最多除颤三次

questions.explanationEn: Severe hypothermia slows the heart to a faint, very slow rhythm that a standard 10-second check can miss, so the BC guideline allows 30–45 seconds to determine pulselessness; starting compressions on a beating hypothermic heart can trigger ventricular fibrillation. If he is truly pulseless, resuscitate: apply the AED and analyse, defibrillate up to three times if indicated, then continue CPR and rapid transport without pausing for further analysis or shocks, because a heart below about 30 °C rarely responds to electricity until it is warmer. Severely hypothermic patients are not actively rewarmed in the field, and resuscitation is never withheld on the basis of cold alone — 'not dead until warm and dead'. The avalanche burial time and any airway packed with snow are important history for the receiving team, not a reason to stop.
questions.explanationZh: 重度低体温会把心跳拖成微弱、极慢的节律，标准的 10 秒检查可能漏掉，所以 BC 考纲允许用 30–45 秒来判断无脉搏；对一颗还在跳的低温心脏做按压，可能诱发室颤。确认无脉搏就复苏：贴 AED 分析，有指征时最多除颤三次，之后继续 CPR 并快速转运，不再为分析或电击暂停——因为低于 30 °C 左右的心脏在变暖之前很少对电击有反应。重度低体温患者在院前不主动复温；也绝不能仅凭「冷」就放弃复苏——「没暖过来就不算死」。雪崩掩埋时间和气道有没有被雪堵住是给接收团队的重要病史，不是停手的理由。

questions.questionEn: A couple in a cabin heated by a propane stove both woke with headache, nausea and dizziness. Standard pulse oximetry reads 98% on both. Why can this reading not be used to rule out carbon monoxide poisoning?
questions.questionZh: 一对夫妇住在用丙烷炉取暖的小木屋里，早上醒来都头痛、恶心、头晕。普通脉搏血氧仪两人都显示 98%。为什么不能用这个读数排除一氧化碳中毒？

options.en: Pulse oximeters read inaccurately in a cold, unheated cabin
options.zh: 脉搏血氧仪在寒冷无暖气的木屋里不准

options.en: Standard oximetry cannot separate carboxyhemoglobin from oxyhemoglobin
options.zh: 普通血氧仪分不清碳氧血红蛋白和氧合血红蛋白

options.en: Carbon monoxide slows the respiratory rate, which raises the saturation
options.zh: 一氧化碳减慢呼吸频率，从而让血氧升高

options.en: Headache and nausea with normal saturation point to a viral illness instead
options.zh: 头痛恶心而血氧正常，提示是病毒感染

questions.explanationEn: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin more than 200 times more avidly than oxygen, forming carboxyhemoglobin that cannot carry oxygen to tissues. A two-wavelength pulse oximeter reads carboxyhemoglobin as if it were oxygenated hemoglobin, so saturation looks normal or even high while the patient is profoundly hypoxic at the cellular level; a CO-oximeter with extra wavelengths measures SpCO directly. Two or more people in one enclosed space with the same flu-like symptoms is CO until proven otherwise. Management: get everyone out, give oxygen by non-rebreather at 15 L/min regardless of the SpO₂ reading (the BC guideline names the non-rebreather for CO poisoning and smoke inhalation), and transport. The AET course pairs this with cyanide from house fires, which instead blocks the cells' use of oxygen, so both can coexist in a fire victim.
questions.explanationZh: 一氧化碳和血红蛋白的结合力是氧的 200 多倍，形成的碳氧血红蛋白无法把氧带给组织。双波长的普通脉搏血氧仪把碳氧血红蛋白当成氧合血红蛋白来读，所以患者细胞层面已经严重缺氧，血氧却显示正常甚至偏高；带额外波长的 CO 血氧仪才能直接测 SpCO。同一密闭空间里两人以上出现同样的「流感样」症状，在证明不是之前就当一氧化碳中毒。处理：所有人撤出，不管 SpO₂ 读数多少都用非重复呼吸面罩 15 L/min 给氧（BC 考纲点名非重复呼吸面罩用于一氧化碳中毒和吸入烟雾），然后转运。AET 课上把它和房屋火灾的氰化物放在一起讲：氰化物阻断的是细胞利用氧的能力，火灾伤员两者可以同时存在。

questions.questionEn: A man escaped a kitchen fire with only a palm-sized partial-thickness burn on one hand, but his eyebrows and nasal hairs are singed, his voice is hoarse and he is coughing up black-flecked sputum. SpO₂ 96%. He wants to drive himself to a clinic. How should you categorise and manage him?
questions.questionZh: 一名男子从厨房火灾中逃出，只有一只手上有巴掌大的部分厚度烧伤，但他的眉毛和鼻毛烧焦、声音嘶哑、咳出带黑点的痰。SpO₂ 96%。他想自己开车去诊所。你该怎么归类和处理？

options.en: Minor burn; dress the hand and let him attend the clinic himself
options.zh: 轻微烧伤；包扎手部，让他自己去诊所

options.en: Stable; a 1% burn does not meet any rapid-transport criterion
options.zh: 稳定；1% 的烧伤不符合任何快速转运标准

options.en: Unstable (airway burns): oxygen, ALS intercept, rapid transport
options.zh: 不稳定（气道烧伤）：给氧、ALS 会合、快速转运

options.en: Stable now; advise him to call back if his voice gets worse
options.zh: 目前稳定；交代他声音变差再打电话

questions.explanationEn: The tiny skin burn is a distraction. Singed facial and nasal hair, hoarseness and carbonaceous sputum are the classic signs of thermal and chemical injury to the upper airway, and swelling can close that airway over the next minutes to hours while the SpO₂ still looks fine. The BC examination guidelines list 'facial or airway burns (with or without inhalation injury)' among the anatomical findings that make a patient unstable and in the rapid transport category regardless of burn size. Apply high-flow oxygen (which also treats possible CO exposure), watch for stridor or worsening voice, request ALS because advanced airway management may be needed, and transport without delay. Letting him drive himself or wait for symptoms to worsen is exactly the delay that turns a manageable airway into an impossible one.
questions.explanationZh: 那块小小的皮肤烧伤是个幌子。面部和鼻毛烧焦、声音嘶哑、炭末样痰，是上气道热损伤和化学损伤的经典征象；接下来几分钟到几小时内，水肿可能把气道封死，而 SpO₂ 还显示正常。BC 考纲把「面部或气道烧伤（无论有无吸入性损伤）」列为不稳定的解剖学表现，不论烧伤面积多大都属于快速转运类别。高流量给氧（同时也处理可能的一氧化碳暴露），留意喘鸣或声音恶化，呼叫 ALS 因为可能需要高级气道管理，立即转运。让他自己开车，或者等症状加重再说，正是把一条还能处理的气道拖成无法处理的那种耽搁。

questions.questionEn: A 15-year-old was pulled from a lake after about a minute underwater. He is awake, coughing persistently, with crackles at both bases and SpO₂ 91%. There is no suggestion of a diving or spinal injury. Which management follows the BC drowning guideline?
questions.questionZh: 一名 15 岁少年在水下约一分钟后被从湖里拉上来。他清醒，持续咳嗽，双肺底可闻及湿啰音，SpO₂ 91%。没有跳水或脊柱损伤的迹象。哪种处理符合 BC 的溺水指南？

options.en: Sitting up at rest, dried and warm, oxygen, and consider CPAP or PEEP
options.zh: 静息坐位、擦干保暖、给氧，考虑 CPAP 或 PEEP

options.en: Supine with legs raised, then walk him to the ambulance once he feels better
options.zh: 平躺抬腿，等他好些再自己走上救护车

options.en: Abdominal thrusts to expel swallowed water before giving oxygen
options.zh: 先做腹部冲击排出吞下的水，再给氧

options.en: Release him to his parents with advice to rest, since he is conscious
options.zh: 他清醒，交给父母带回休息即可

questions.explanationEn: The BC Drowning/Near Drowning guideline directs: spinal motion restriction only if the mechanism suggests it, keep the patient at rest, position sitting up, remove wet clothing and dry the patient, avoid rough handling, maintain body temperature, support failing respirations with positive-pressure ventilation, and for a PCP use PEEP or CPAP if indicated. Crackles and a saturation of 91% after submersion mean aspirated water has already washed out surfactant and alveoli are collapsing; this can worsen over hours even in someone who seems to recover, so every symptomatic submersion victim is transported. Abdominal thrusts delay oxygenation and provoke vomiting; walking and supine positioning increase oxygen demand and worsen the work of breathing. Hypothermia after cold-water immersion is treated at the same time.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的溺水/近溺水指南要求：只在受伤机制提示时才做脊柱活动限制；让患者静息、取坐位、脱掉湿衣擦干、避免粗暴搬动、维持体温；呼吸衰竭时用正压通气支持；PCP 有指征时用 PEEP 或 CPAP。淹没后出现湿啰音和 91% 的血氧，说明吸入的水已经冲掉了表面活性物质、肺泡正在塌陷；即使看起来恢复了，这在接下来几小时也可能恶化，所以有症状的淹没患者一律转运。腹部冲击会耽误给氧并诱发呕吐；走动和平躺会增加耗氧、加重呼吸做功。冷水浸泡后的低体温要同时处理。

questions.questionEn: A scuba diver made a rapid, panicked ascent and within three minutes of surfacing became confused with weakness of the left arm and severe chest and joint pain. He asks for something for the pain. Which analgesic on the BC formulary is contraindicated here, and why?
questions.questionZh: 一名水肺潜水员惊慌中快速上浮，出水后三分钟内出现意识混乱、左臂无力、剧烈的胸痛和关节痛。他要求止痛。BC 药单上哪种镇痛药在这里禁用？为什么？

options.en: Acetaminophen, because it masks neurological deterioration
options.zh: 对乙酰氨基酚，因为它会掩盖神经功能恶化

options.en: Ibuprofen, because it increases bleeding into the affected joints
options.zh: 布洛芬，因为它增加受累关节内出血

options.en: Methoxyflurane, because it is contraindicated below 18 years of age
options.zh: 甲氧氟烷，因为 18 岁以下禁用

options.en: Entonox, because nitrous oxide expands trapped gas bubbles
options.zh: 安桃乐，因为氧化亚氮会让被困气泡膨胀

questions.explanationEn: Rapid ascent with immediate neurological symptoms points to arterial gas embolism from pulmonary over-expansion, possibly with decompression sickness; both involve gas bubbles in tissues and blood vessels. Nitrous oxide is far more soluble than nitrogen, so it moves into any gas-filled space and expands it, which is why the BC Entonox monograph lists decompression sickness, air embolism and pneumothorax among its contraindications. The correct care is high-concentration oxygen by non-rebreather (to wash out nitrogen and shrink bubbles), supine positioning, keeping him warm and still, and urgent transport toward a facility that can arrange hyperbaric treatment, with dive details (depth, time, ascent) handed over. Acetaminophen and ibuprofen are not contraindicated for this reason, and the age restriction on methoxyflurane is irrelevant to an adult diver.
questions.explanationZh: 快速上浮后立刻出现神经症状，指向肺过度膨胀引起的动脉气体栓塞，可能合并减压病；两者都是组织和血管里有气泡。氧化亚氮的溶解度远高于氮气，会钻进任何含气腔隙并把它撑大，所以 BC 的安桃乐药物专论把减压病、空气栓塞和气胸列为禁忌。正确的处理是非重复呼吸面罩高浓度给氧（冲洗氮气、缩小气泡）、仰卧、保暖、保持安静，并紧急转运到能安排高压氧治疗的机构，交接时带上潜水资料（深度、时间、上浮过程）。对乙酰氨基酚和布洛芬不会因这个原因被禁；甲氧氟烷的年龄限制和一个成年潜水员无关。

questions.questionEn: A construction worker has had both legs pinned under a concrete slab for five hours. Rescue crews are 15 minutes from lifting it. He is alert, in pain, HR 112, BP 118/76. Why does the AET course teach that a PCP should establish IV access and start fluids before the slab comes off, and what rhythm complication should you be ready for?
questions.questionZh: 一名建筑工人双腿被混凝土板压住已五小时，救援队还有 15 分钟就能抬起板子。他清醒、疼痛，HR 112，BP 118/76。为什么 AET 课上教 PCP 要在板子抬起之前建立静脉通路并开始补液？你要准备应对什么心律并发症？

options.en: To control pain; the main risk after release is fat embolism
options.zh: 为了止痛；释放后的主要风险是脂肪栓塞

options.en: Release floods the circulation with potassium and myoglobin; fluids dilute them
options.zh: 释放后钾和肌红蛋白涌入循环；补液可以稀释它们

options.en: To raise his systolic pressure above 140 so he tolerates extrication
options.zh: 把收缩压升到 140 以上，让他能承受脱困

options.en: It is unnecessary; his pressure is normal, so fluids can safely wait until hospital
options.zh: 没有必要；血压正常，补液完全可以等到医院再说

questions.explanationEn: While the slab is in place the crushed muscle is isolated from the circulation; it is dying, leaking potassium, myoglobin, phosphate and lactic acid into the trapped limb. The moment the weight lifts, that load is washed into the central circulation. Hyperkalemia can stop the heart within minutes (peaked T waves, widening QRS, then VF or asystole), and myoglobin precipitates in the renal tubules to cause acute kidney injury. That is why the course — reflecting BCEHS practice — wants vascular access and crystalloid running before release when extrication is prolonged, with the cardiac monitor on and ALS requested. His normal blood pressure is irrelevant to the reperfusion risk. On the EMALB licensing exam, fluid administration is framed through the hypovolemia protocol (20 mL/kg boluses to a maximum of 2 litres, reassessing every 500 mL) and the crushed or mangled extremity places him in the rapid transport category; the pre-release timing is AET/BCEHS teaching rather than a stated exam-guideline step.
questions.explanationZh: 板子压着时，被压碎的肌肉和循环是隔开的；它正在坏死，把钾、肌红蛋白、磷酸盐和乳酸渗进被困的肢体里。重物一抬起，这一整包东西就被冲进中心循环。高钾血症几分钟内就能让心脏停跳（T 波高尖、QRS 增宽，然后室颤或心搏停止），肌红蛋白则在肾小管里沉淀导致急性肾损伤。所以课上——反映的是 BCEHS 的做法——要求在长时间脱困的情况下，释放前就建好血管通路、把晶体液输上，心电监护开着并呼叫 ALS。他的血压正常和再灌注风险无关。在 EMALB 执照考试里，补液是按低血容量流程来框定的（每次 20 mL/kg、最多 2 升、每 500 mL 重评），而压碎或毁损的肢体让他属于快速转运类别；「释放前就开始」这个时机是 AET/BCEHS 的教学内容，不是考纲明文写出的步骤。

questions.questionEn: Six hours after a closed tibial fracture was splinted, a 22-year-old reports escalating calf pain that analgesics barely touch. The calf is tense and the pain becomes severe when you gently flex his toes upward. Pedal pulses are present and the foot is warm. Which statement is correct?
questions.questionZh: 一名 22 岁患者闭合性胫骨骨折夹板固定六小时后，诉小腿疼痛不断加剧，止痛药几乎没用。小腿紧绷，你轻轻把他的脚趾向上扳时疼痛剧烈。足背动脉搏动存在，足部温暖。哪句说法正确？

options.en: A palpable pulse excludes compartment syndrome; increase the analgesia
options.zh: 能摸到脉搏就排除了筋膜室综合征；加大镇痛

options.en: Elevate the leg well above the heart and reassess the swelling in an hour
options.zh: 把腿抬得远高于心脏，一小时后复评肿胀

options.en: Early compartment syndrome; loosen the splint, limb at heart level, transport
options.zh: 早期筋膜室综合征；松开夹板、肢体平心脏、转运

options.en: Apply a firmer compression bandage to control the bleeding inside the calf
options.zh: 缠更紧的加压绷带控制小腿内部出血

questions.explanationEn: Compartment syndrome is pressure rising inside a closed fascial space until it chokes off capillary perfusion to muscle and nerve. The first and most reliable signs are pain far beyond what the injury should produce and pain on passive stretch of the muscles in that compartment; paresthesia follows. Pulselessness, pallor and paralysis are late findings — by the time a pulse disappears, irreversible damage is usually under way — so a present pulse never excludes the diagnosis. Field management is to remove anything that constricts (tight splint straps, circumferential dressings), keep the limb at heart level (elevation above the heart lowers arterial inflow and worsens ischemia), avoid further compression, give analgesia, and get him to surgical care quickly, because fasciotomy is the only definitive treatment.
questions.explanationZh: 筋膜室综合征是封闭筋膜腔内压力不断升高，直到掐断对肌肉和神经的毛细血管灌注。最早、最可靠的征象是远超伤情应有程度的疼痛，以及被动牵拉该筋膜室肌肉时的疼痛；随后出现感觉异常。无脉、苍白、瘫痪都是晚期表现——脉搏消失时，不可逆损伤通常已经在发生——所以摸得到脉搏永远不能排除这个诊断。院前处理是解除一切压迫（过紧的夹板绑带、环形敷料），肢体保持在心脏水平（抬高过心脏会减少动脉灌注、加重缺血），避免再加压，给予镇痛，并尽快送到外科——筋膜切开是唯一的根本治疗。

questions.questionEn: On the second night at a 3,600-m hut a hiker who had a headache and nausea all day is now stumbling like a drunk and cannot answer simple questions. He has not been drinking alcohol. What is the most likely diagnosis and the single most important intervention?
questions.questionZh: 在海拔 3,600 米的山屋过第二夜时，一名白天一直头痛恶心的徒步者现在走路像醉汉一样跌跌撞撞，回答不了简单的问题。他没有喝酒。最可能的诊断是什么？最重要的一项干预是什么？

options.en: High-altitude cerebral edema; descend immediately, oxygen meanwhile
options.zh: 高原脑水肿；立即下撤，同时给氧

options.en: Acute mountain sickness; rest overnight at this altitude and reassess
options.zh: 急性高山病；在此海拔休息过夜再评估

options.en: High-altitude pulmonary edema; sit him upright and give a bronchodilator
options.zh: 高原肺水肿；坐直并给支气管扩张剂

options.en: Hypoglycemia; give oral glucose and continue the ascent in the morning
options.zh: 低血糖；口服葡萄糖，早上继续上升

questions.explanationEn: Acute mountain sickness (headache plus nausea, fatigue or poor sleep after recent ascent) is the mild end of the spectrum. The appearance of ataxia or altered mental status in someone with AMS marks progression to high-altitude cerebral edema, which can kill within hours. The AET course's rule is 'descent is the intervention': losing even a few hundred metres of altitude is the definitive treatment, and oxygen is titrated while descent is organised. High-altitude pulmonary edema presents with breathlessness at rest, cough and crackles, and is treated with high-flow oxygen plus descent; a bronchodilator is not the fix. Checking a glucose is reasonable in any altered patient ('glucose first'), but staying at altitude or climbing higher in the morning with these signs would be a fatal plan.
questions.explanationZh: 急性高山病（近期上升后出现头痛，加上恶心、乏力或睡眠差）是这条谱系的轻端。AMS 患者出现共济失调或精神状态改变，标志着进展为高原脑水肿，可在数小时内致死。AET 课上的原则是「下撤就是治疗」：哪怕只下降几百米也是根本治疗，组织下撤的同时滴定给氧。高原肺水肿表现为静息气促、咳嗽和湿啰音，用高流量氧加下撤来处理，支气管扩张剂解决不了问题。任何意识改变的患者查血糖都是合理的（「先查血糖」），但带着这些征象留在原海拔，或者早上继续上升，是致命的计划。

questions.questionEn: A time-critical patient is at a rural clinic. What is the key principle when deciding between helicopter and ground transport?
questions.questionZh: 一名时间紧迫的患者在乡村诊所。在直升机和地面转运之间做决定时，核心原则是什么？

options.en: Air is always faster, so request a helicopter whenever one is available
options.zh: 空运总是更快，有直升机就请求

options.en: Compare total time to definitive care, not just travel time
options.zh: 比较到达确定性治疗的总时间，而不只是路上时间

options.en: Ground is preferred unless the patient is in cardiac arrest
options.zh: 除非患者心脏骤停，否则优先地面转运

options.en: Choose the mode the family prefers once the risks have been explained
options.zh: 向家属解释风险后按家属的意愿选择

questions.explanationEn: A helicopter's speed in the air is only one part of the equation. Total time to definitive care includes crew activation, flight to the scene, landing-zone set-up, patient packaging and loading, the flight itself, and the transfer at the other end — and weather or darkness can cancel the mission after you have waited for it. The AET course's rule is to run the two timelines side by side: request air early when the numbers favour it, keep treating and packaging, and have a ground plan ready so that a weather turn-down costs nothing. Air is not automatically faster for short distances or when a landing zone is far from the patient; cardiac arrest is actually a poor indication for flight because effective CPR in a small cabin is difficult; and transport mode is a clinical decision, not a family preference.
questions.explanationZh: 直升机在空中的速度只是算式的一部分。到达确定性治疗的总时间包括机组启动、飞到现场、布置着陆区、患者包扎装载、飞行本身，以及另一端的交接——而天气或夜间可能在你等了半天之后把任务取消。AET 课上的原则是把两条时间线并排算：数字有利时尽早请求空运，同时继续处置和打包，并准备好地面方案，这样天气拒飞时什么也不损失。距离短或着陆区离患者很远时，空运并不自动更快；心脏骤停其实是飞行的差指征，因为在狭小机舱里做有效 CPR 很困难；转运方式是临床决定，不是家属偏好。

questions.questionEn: You are driving a stable 80-year-old with a hip fracture down a mountain highway in freezing rain when you feel the rear of the ambulance slide on a curve. What is the correct response?
questions.questionZh: 你载着一位生命体征稳定、髋部骨折的 80 岁老人，在冻雨中沿山区公路下行，过弯时感觉车尾打滑。正确的应对是什么？

options.en: Slow down, increase following distance and drive without lights and siren
options.zh: 减速、拉大车距，不开警灯警笛正常行驶

options.en: Keep your speed up to reach hospital before the conditions worsen further
options.zh: 保持车速，趁路况进一步恶化前赶到医院

options.en: Activate lights and siren so other drivers give you more room
options.zh: 开警灯警笛让其他司机给你让出更多空间

options.en: Pull onto the shoulder and wait for a police escort before going on
options.zh: 停到路肩等警车护送再继续

questions.explanationEn: The ambulance is the most dangerous place a stable patient will be all day. A slide on a curve means the tyres have already lost grip; the only correct answers are to reduce speed smoothly, lengthen the gap to traffic ahead, avoid sudden steering or braking, and if conditions remain unsafe, stop somewhere safe until they improve. A stable hip fracture gives no clinical reason to accept extra risk, so lights and siren (which raise speed and reduce the margin for error without creating traction) are not justified. 'Hurrying before it gets worse' is how ambulances end up in the ditch, and a police escort does not change the road surface. The course's defensive-driving principle is that a crash converts one patient into three.
questions.explanationZh: 对一个稳定的患者来说，救护车是他这一天里最危险的地方。过弯打滑说明轮胎已经失去抓地力；唯一正确的做法是平顺减速、拉大与前车的距离、避免急打方向或急刹，如果路况仍不安全就在安全的地方停下等待好转。稳定的髋部骨折没有任何临床理由去承担额外风险，所以警灯警笛（只会提高车速、压缩容错空间，却不会增加抓地力）站不住脚。「趁还没变得更糟赶紧开」正是救护车冲进沟里的方式；警车护送也改变不了路面。课上防御性驾驶的原则是：一次车祸把一个患者变成三个。

questions.questionEn: You must choose a daytime landing zone for an air ambulance near a rural crash. Which site is the most suitable?
questions.questionZh: 你要在一起乡村车祸附近为空中救护选一个白天的着陆区。哪个场地最合适？

options.en: A 20 m × 20 m gravel lot beside the highway, bordered by a line of utility poles
options.zh: 公路旁 20 m × 20 m 的碎石场地，边上一排电线杆

options.en: A freshly ploughed field, 40 m square, with loose soil and standing dust
options.zh: 刚犁过的 40 m 见方的田地，土松、扬尘

options.en: A sloped hayfield, 35 m square, with a 15-degree grade and tall grass
options.zh: 坡度 15 度、长着高草的 35 m 见方的干草地

options.en: A level, firm 30 m × 30 m paved area, free of wires and loose debris
options.zh: 平整坚实的 30 m × 30 m 铺装场地，无电线、无松散杂物

questions.explanationEn: The standard the course teaches is roughly 30 m × 30 m (100 ft × 100 ft) by day, larger at night, on firm, level ground with no more than a gentle slope, clear of wires, poles, trees, loose debris and people, and away from traffic. The gravel lot is too small and sits under utility lines, the single most lethal landing-zone hazard. The ploughed field is big enough but loose soil and dust cause brown-out, blinding the pilot on approach, and soft ground can let a skid sink. A 15-degree slope is well beyond what most helicopters can safely land on, and tall grass hides holes and obstacles. Once the site is chosen, mark the corners, note the wind direction, keep everyone at least 30 m back, and brief the flight crew.
questions.explanationZh: 课上教的标准是白天约 30 m × 30 m（100 英尺见方），夜间更大，地面坚实平整、坡度不超过缓坡，没有电线、电杆、树木、松散杂物和人员，并远离车流。碎石场地太小，而且在电线下方——电线是着陆区最致命的单一危险。犁过的田地够大，但松土和扬尘会造成「褐视」，让飞行员在进近时看不见，软地还可能让滑橇陷下去。15 度的坡远超大多数直升机能安全着陆的范围，高草还会藏住坑洞和障碍。选定场地后，标出四角、记下风向、让所有人退到至少 30 m 以外，并向飞行机组通报。

questions.questionEn: The helicopter has landed on a gentle hillside with rotors still turning, and you need to bring the patient to it. From where, and when, should you approach?
questions.questionZh: 直升机在一个缓坡上着陆，旋翼还在转，你需要把患者送过去。你应该从哪里、在什么时候接近？

options.en: From the uphill side, where the ground is closest to the cabin door
options.zh: 从上坡侧，那里地面离舱门最近

options.en: From directly behind, keeping clear of the pilot's forward field of view
options.zh: 从正后方接近，避开飞行员前方视野

options.en: From the downhill side, in the pilot's view, only after the crew signals
options.zh: 从下坡侧、在飞行员视野内，机组示意后才接近

options.en: From any side as soon as the skids touch, keeping your head down
options.zh: 滑橇一落地就从任何一侧低头接近

questions.explanationEn: Three rules govern approaching a running helicopter: wait for a clear signal from the pilot or crew, approach from the front or side where the pilot can see you, and never go near the tail rotor, which spins too fast to see. On a slope there is a fourth: approach from the downhill side, because on the uphill side the main rotor disc is closer to the ground and can strike a standing person. Crouch, do not run, carry long objects horizontally below waist height, secure hats, sheets and loose cords, and let the crew direct loading. Approaching from behind puts you in the tail-rotor arc and out of the pilot's sight; approaching the moment the skids touch, before a signal, is how ground crews are injured.
questions.explanationZh: 接近旋翼运转中的直升机有三条规矩：等飞行员或机组给出明确手势；从前方或侧方、飞行员看得见你的方向接近；绝不靠近尾桨——它转得快到肉眼看不见。在坡地上还有第四条：从下坡侧接近，因为上坡侧主旋翼桨盘离地面更近，可能打到站立的人。压低身体、不要跑、长物件横着拿在腰部以下、固定好帽子、床单和松散的线缆，装载听机组指挥。从后方接近等于走进尾桨范围、又在飞行员视线之外；滑橇一落地、还没等手势就冲上去，正是地面人员受伤的方式。

questions.questionEn: A trauma patient with a splinted forearm is loaded into an unpressurised helicopter that will climb about 1,500 m. Which piece of equipment needs attention because of the altitude change?
questions.questionZh: 一名前臂夹板固定的创伤患者被装上一架无增压直升机，将爬升约 1,500 米。因为海拔变化，哪件器材需要特别留意？

options.en: The cardiac monitor, whose battery drains faster at altitude
options.zh: 心电监护仪，高空耗电更快

options.en: An inflatable air splint, whose pressure rises as trapped gas expands
options.zh: 充气夹板，被困气体膨胀使压力升高

options.en: The pulse oximeter, which reads falsely high in the cold cabin
options.zh: 脉搏血氧仪，在寒冷的舱内读数假性偏高

options.en: The oxygen regulator, which delivers less flow per litre setting at altitude
options.zh: 氧气流量调节器，同一流量档输出变少

questions.explanationEn: Boyle's law: as atmospheric pressure falls with altitude, a fixed amount of gas occupies more volume. Any closed gas space grows — an air splint tightens and can act as a tourniquet, an endotracheal tube cuff over-inflates, gas in the bowel or a pneumothorax expands, and air in IV bags and drip chambers distorts gravity flow rates. Before flight the AET course teaches you to release some air from inflatable splints (or swap to a rigid splint), vent tubes, check cuff pressures, and warn the flight crew about any trapped gas. Monitor batteries and oxygen regulators are not meaningfully affected by a 1,500-m climb, and cold makes pulse oximetry unreliable or falsely low through poor perfusion, not falsely high.
questions.explanationZh: 波义耳定律：随着海拔升高大气压下降，同样多的气体占据更大的体积。任何封闭的含气腔都会变大——充气夹板越绷越紧、可能变成止血带，气管导管套囊过度充气，肠道里的气体或气胸扩张，输液袋和滴壶里的空气也会让靠重力的滴速失真。AET 课上教的是起飞前给充气夹板放掉一些气（或换成硬夹板）、把各种管路开放排气、检查套囊压力，并把任何被困气体的情况告知飞行机组。监护仪电池和氧气调节器不会被 1,500 米的爬升明显影响；寒冷让脉搏血氧仪因灌注差而不可靠或假性偏低，而不是偏高。

questions.questionEn: A 72-year-old with COPD and pneumonia has SpO₂ 90% on 2 L/min by nasal cannula at sea level. He will be flown in an unpressurised helicopter cruising at about 2,000 m. What should you anticipate?
questions.questionZh: 一名 72 岁 COPD 合并肺炎的患者，在海平面鼻导管 2 L/min 下 SpO₂ 90%。他将乘无增压直升机在约 2,000 米巡航。你应该预见什么？

options.en: No change; the supplemental oxygen fully offsets the altitude effect
options.zh: 不用变；吸氧已经完全抵消了海拔影响

options.en: Reduce the oxygen to protect his hypoxic drive at altitude
options.zh: 减少吸氧，在高空保护他的缺氧驱动

options.en: Expect his saturation to rise because the air is cleaner
options.zh: 预计血氧会上升，因为空气更干净

options.en: Expect desaturation as partial pressure falls; increase oxygen
options.zh: 预计氧分压下降导致血氧下降；增加吸氧

questions.explanationEn: Dalton's law: the fraction of oxygen in air stays at 21%, but as barometric pressure falls with altitude the partial pressure of oxygen falls with it, so less oxygen is driven into the blood. A healthy passenger compensates easily; a patient already sitting at 90% on the steep part of the oxyhemoglobin curve has no reserve and will desaturate as the aircraft climbs. The pre-flight plan is to increase the FiO₂ (and have a mask ready), monitor continuously with pulse oximetry and capnography, and tell the flight crew. Cutting oxygen to 'protect hypoxic drive' is dangerous at any altitude; the BC guideline for COPD titrates oxygen to the patient rather than withholding it. Cleaner air does not add oxygen molecules.
questions.explanationZh: 道尔顿定律：空气中氧气的比例始终是 21%，但随着海拔升高气压下降，氧分压也跟着下降，被压进血液的氧就更少。健康乘客轻松代偿；一个已经停在 90%、处在氧合血红蛋白解离曲线陡峭段的患者没有任何储备，飞机一爬升就会掉血氧。起飞前的计划是提高吸入氧浓度（备好面罩）、用脉搏血氧和二氧化碳图持续监测，并告知飞行机组。为了「保护缺氧驱动」而减氧在任何海拔都危险；BC 考纲对 COPD 的做法是按患者情况滴定给氧，而不是不给。空气更干净并不会多出氧分子。

questions.questionEn: Noise and vibration inside a helicopter make some assessments unreliable. Which combination remains dependable for monitoring a patient in flight?
questions.questionZh: 直升机舱内的噪音和振动让一些评估变得不可靠。哪一组监测手段在飞行中仍然靠得住？

options.en: Pulse oximetry, waveform capnography and the ECG monitor
options.zh: 脉搏血氧、波形二氧化碳图和心电监护

options.en: Auscultation of breath sounds with a standard stethoscope
options.zh: 用普通听诊器听呼吸音

options.en: Palpation of a radial pulse to count the heart rate
options.zh: 触诊桡动脉数心率

options.en: Counting respirations by watching chest rise under the blankets
options.zh: 隔着毯子看胸廓起伏数呼吸

questions.explanationEn: Rotor noise defeats the stethoscope entirely — you cannot hear breath sounds, heart sounds or a Korotkoff pulse for a manual blood pressure — and vibration makes palpating a pulse or watching subtle chest movement unreliable. That is why air crews depend on electronic monitoring: continuous SpO₂, waveform capnography (which also confirms ventilation and airway device placement), ECG and automated non-invasive blood pressure, all set to alarm. The AET course adds the practical corollary: finish every assessment that needs your ears or hands before the aircraft starts, secure all leads and tubes, and plan how you will recognise deterioration from the monitors alone.
questions.explanationZh: 旋翼噪音让听诊器完全失效——听不到呼吸音、心音，也听不到手动量血压的柯氏音——振动则让触诊脉搏或观察细微的胸廓起伏都不可靠。所以空中机组依赖电子监测：持续 SpO₂、波形二氧化碳图（同时能确认通气和气道装置位置）、心电图和自动无创血压，并全部设好报警。AET 课上补了一个实际推论：所有需要用耳朵和手的评估都在飞机启动前做完，固定好所有导线和管路，并事先想好如何只凭监护仪识别病情恶化。

questions.questionEn: The air ambulance is ten minutes out and asks for your landing-zone report. What information does the flight crew need from you before they commit to the approach?
questions.questionZh: 空中救护还有十分钟到达，请你报告着陆区情况。飞行机组在决定进近之前需要你提供什么信息？

options.en: The patient's full SAMPLE history and the last two sets of vital signs
options.zh: 患者完整的 SAMPLE 病史和最近两套生命体征

options.en: The names of all crew on scene and the ambulance unit number
options.zh: 现场所有人员姓名和救护车编号

options.en: LZ location, surface and size, hazards, wind direction and marking
options.zh: 着陆区位置、地面和尺寸、危险、风向和标记方式

options.en: The receiving hospital's bed availability and the attending physician
options.zh: 接收医院的床位情况和主治医生

questions.explanationEn: The pilot is making a flying decision, so the report is about the ground, not the patient: exact location (GPS or a clear landmark), the surface and dimensions, every hazard — wires, poles, towers, trees, slopes, loose debris, livestock, people — the wind direction and strength, how the zone is marked, and the radio channel for the ground contact. A patient report follows later in a structured MIST handover once the medical crew is ready to receive it. Crew names and unit numbers are administrative, and hospital bed status is the dispatcher's and flight crew's problem, not information they need to land safely.
questions.explanationZh: 飞行员要做的是飞行决定，所以这份报告讲的是地面，不是患者：确切位置（GPS 或清楚的地标）、地面类型和尺寸、所有危险——电线、电杆、铁塔、树木、坡度、松散杂物、牲畜、人员——风向风力、着陆区的标记方式，以及地面联络的无线电频道。患者情况等医疗机组准备好接收时，再用结构化的 MIST 交接。人员姓名和车辆编号是行政信息；医院床位是调度和飞行机组要操心的事，不是他们安全着陆所需的信息。

questions.questionEn: A stabbing victim has a chest seal over a right-sided wound and clinical signs of a simple pneumothorax. He is awaiting helicopter transfer and remains stable on oxygen. Within the scope tested on the BC licensing exam, what should a PCP do about the risk of gas expansion in flight?
questions.questionZh: 一名刀刺伤患者右胸伤口上覆着胸封，有单纯性气胸的临床表现。他正等待直升机转运，吸氧下仍然稳定。在 BC 执照考试所考的执业范围内，PCP 针对飞行中气体膨胀的风险该怎么做？

options.en: Perform needle decompression before takeoff to prevent tensioning
options.zh: 起飞前做针刺减压，防止张力性气胸

options.en: Notify the flight crew, give oxygen, be ready to relieve the chest seal
options.zh: 通知飞行机组，给氧，随时准备松开胸封

options.en: Replace the three-sided dressing with a fully occlusive one for the flight
options.zh: 把三面敷料换成完全封闭的敷料再上飞机

options.en: Request ground transport only; pneumothorax patients cannot fly
options.zh: 只走地面转运；气胸患者不能坐飞机

questions.explanationEn: As the aircraft climbs, the air in his pleural space will expand and a simple pneumothorax can become a tension pneumothorax. The PCP's job is to anticipate it: brief the flight crew clearly so they can plan (they carry the equipment and scope for decompression), keep him on high-flow oxygen, monitor for rising respiratory distress, falling SpO₂, tracheal deviation or hypotension, and be ready to lift or 'burp' the chest seal to release pressure — the BC examination guidelines' chest-trauma protocol says to monitor for tension pneumothorax and relieve it by that means. Needle decompression is not within the PCP scope tested by EMALB (the AET course teaches it as BCEHS practice, and the school's own quiz offers it as an option), so on the exam it is the wrong answer. Sealing the wound completely removes the vent you would need, and a pneumothorax is a reason to prepare for flight, not an absolute bar to it.
questions.explanationZh: 飞机爬升时，他胸膜腔里的空气会膨胀，单纯性气胸可能变成张力性气胸。PCP 的任务是预见它：向飞行机组讲清楚让他们提前计划（减压的器材和执业范围在他们那里），维持高流量吸氧，监测呼吸窘迫加重、SpO₂ 下降、气管偏移或低血压，并随时准备掀开或「放气」胸封释放压力——BC 考纲的胸部创伤流程写的就是监测张力性气胸并用这种方式解除。针刺减压不在 EMALB 考核的 PCP 范围内（AET 课上把它当作 BCEHS 的做法来教，学校自己的测验也把它列为选项），所以在考试里它是错误答案。把伤口完全封死等于拿掉了你需要的排气口；气胸是飞行前要做准备的理由，不是绝对禁飞。

questions.questionEn: It is 02:00 and the helicopter is five minutes out. A firefighter asks how to light the landing zone. Which plan is correct?
questions.questionZh: 凌晨两点，直升机还有五分钟到。一名消防员问你着陆区该怎么打光。哪个方案正确？

options.en: Point all vehicle high beams and spotlights at the approaching helicopter
options.zh: 把所有车辆远光灯和探照灯对准接近中的直升机

options.en: Use the ambulance's strobing emergency lights as the only marker
options.zh: 只用救护车的频闪警灯做标记

options.en: Have bystanders hold flashlights at each corner facing the aircraft
options.zh: 让旁观者在四角举手电筒对着飞机

options.en: Mark the corners with low-intensity lights; keep beams off the aircraft
options.zh: 用低亮度灯光标出四角，光束不要照飞机

questions.explanationEn: At night the pilot is often flying on night-vision goggles or dark-adapted eyes, and a bright light aimed at the aircraft causes flash-blindness at the most critical moment. The zone should be outlined by low-intensity markers at the corners (chemical light sticks, cones with lights, or vehicle low beams angled down into the zone and never upward), with strobes and spotlights off or turned away as the aircraft approaches. People do not belong on the corners of an active landing zone, and the zone itself must be larger than by day because obstacles are harder to see. Follow any lighting instructions the pilot gives by radio, and keep everyone well back until the crew signals.
questions.explanationZh: 夜间飞行员常常戴着夜视镜或靠暗适应的眼睛飞，一束对准飞机的强光会在最关键的时刻造成闪光致盲。着陆区应当用低亮度标记物在四角勾出轮廓（化学荧光棒、带灯的锥筒，或车辆近光灯向下照进区内、绝不向上），飞机进近时关掉或转开频闪灯和探照灯。活动中的着陆区四角不该站人，而且夜间的着陆区要比白天更大，因为障碍物更难看见。飞行员通过无线电给出的任何打光指示都要照办，机组示意前所有人都退得远远的。
